title: Bidirectional A* 🔍 Finds Routes from Both Ends!
description: Watch Bidirectional A* sweep through a real street-map graph, expanding intelligently from start and goal at the same time. When the two search frontiers meet, the route is stitched together with A*-style heuristics for fast, optimal paths.
ig_caption:
🧭✨ Reykjavík’s street grid becomes a weighted graph—nodes are intersections, edges are road segments.

🔁 Bidirectional A* runs two coordinated A* searches: one forward from the start and one backward from the goal. Each side uses an admissible heuristic to prioritize promising expansions, and the moment the frontiers intersect, we reconstruct the optimal path by combining the partial routes. That “meet-in-the-middle” strategy often reduces explored area compared to single-direction search—especially on large maps. 🧠⚡

📍Real-world twist: street maps aren’t just lines—they’re graph structures with varying connectivity, turn-like constraints (modeled in the graph), and weighted costs (distance/time). This visualization shows how graph theory + heuristics can turn messy roads into a clean route plan.

✅ Want a version with traffic-like weights or multiple goals? Comment “VARIANTS” and share this reel with a friend learning pathfinding!
